target.title: fix(macos): prevent hatch and web chat from timing out on slow first replies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where macOS onboarding/web chat could make a slow first assistant reply look stuck or prematurely timed out when the selected model takes longer than the old client-side budget. This matters for first-run hatch/chat paths with slower models such as OpenAI 5.5, where the user expects the assistant to keep working after they describe its purpose.

The mismatch was that the macOS WebChat path needed a longer assistant-run budget and a completion observation path, while the request/ACK deadline should still fail quickly when the gateway is unreachable. The macOS GatewayConnection API now names those two timeout concepts separately so future callers do not accidentally treat an ACK deadline as the assistant run budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

This separates the short request/ACK deadline from the actual WebChat assistant run budget. The shared `GatewayConnection.chatSend` default stays request-sized so other macOS callers such as Talk Mode keep their existing timeout policy, while the API now exposes `agentRunTimeoutMs` separately from `requestTimeoutMs`. `MacGatewayChatTransport.sendMessage` explicitly opts WebChat/hatch into a five-minute agent run budget without lengthening the local ACK deadline.

The shared chat UI now reads its pending/completion budget from the transport: default transports keep the existing 120-second pending wait, and macOS WebChat explicitly opts into the five-minute window through `MacGatewayChatTransport.pendingRunTimeoutMs`. macOS WebChat also waits for completion through existing Gateway `agent.wait` before refreshing history. The change uses existing Gateway surfaces (`chat.send.timeoutMs` and `agent.wait`) and does not change gateway protocol shape, auth, provider routing, model selection, session storage, schema, migrations, iOS transport behavior, or delivery channels.

## User Impact

macOS users hatching or chatting with a newly configured assistant now get a realistic wait window and a production completion observation path for slow first replies instead of a premature timeout or stuck-looking state while the assistant run may still be active or recently completed.

The intended behavior is that macOS WebChat/hatch keeps gateway ACK failures prompt while giving only the WebChat assistant run, UI pending state, and completion refresh path the first-run-sized five-minute window. Shared/default chat transports keep the existing 120-second pending budget unless they explicitly opt into a longer one.

## Evidence

Native macOS visual/accessibility proof on the PR build, using the native `OpenClaw Chat` window and a session-level `openai/gpt-5.3-codex-spark` override for this proof run:

```text
submitted_at_local=2026-07-05 14:48:31 CST
prompt=For local PR #97722 native WebChat visual proof only: use the shell tool to run exactly `sleep 45` with no output, then reply exactly `native WebChat slow reply proof complete`.
```

At +32 seconds, the native macOS window was still connected and still showed the assistant pending state instead of a 30-second timeout/error:

```text
pending_capture_at_local=2026-07-05 14:49:03 CST
AXWindow name='OpenClaw Chat' desc='standard window'
  AXGroup
    AXScrollArea
      AXOpaqueProviderGroup desc='list'
        AXStaticText value='For local PR #97722 native WebChat visual proof only: use the shell tool to run exactly sleep 45 with no output, then reply exactly native WebChat slow reply proof complete.'
        AXStaticText value='Agent avatar'
        AXStaticText value='Writing'
    AXStaticText value='Gateway connected'
```

After the slow run completed, the same native window cleared the pending state and showed the final assistant reply:

```text
completion_capture_at_local=2026-07-05 14:49:38 CST
AXWindow name='OpenClaw Chat' desc='standard window'
  AXGroup
    AXScrollArea
      AXOpaqueProviderGroup desc='list'
        AXStaticText value='For local PR #97722 native WebChat visual proof only: use the shell tool to run exactly sleep 45 with no output, then reply exactly native WebChat slow reply proof complete.'
        AXStaticText value='Agent avatar'
        AXStaticText value='native WebChat slow reply proof complete'
    AXStaticText value='Gateway connected'
```

Post-scope validation for this follow-up commit:

```text
followup_head=5e44632976
swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter ChatViewModelTests
result: 107 tests in 1 suite passed

swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter GatewayConnectionControlTests
result: 9 tests in 1 suite passed
```

Timeout-scope regression coverage after the scope fix:

- `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Tests/OpenClawKitTests/ChatViewModelTests.swift` asserts the shared/default completion wait uses `120_000` ms and that a transport opt-in is propagated as `300_000` ms.
- `apps/macos/Tests/OpenClawIPCTests/GatewayConnectionControlTests.swift` asserts the low-level `GatewayConnection.chatSend` default remains `timeoutMs == 30000`, explicit `agentRunTimeoutMs` controls the gateway `chat.send.timeoutMs` parameter, `MacGatewayChatTransport.pendingRunTimeoutMs == 300_000`, `MacGatewayChatTransport.sendMessage` sends `timeoutMs == 300_000`, and `agent.wait` receives the supplied run ID and timeout.
- `apps/ios/Sources/Chat/IOSGatewayChatTransport.swift` is unchanged, so iOS continues to use its existing `30000` chat-send timeout and inherits the shared/default pending budget.
target.author: zhangguiping-xydt
